event_checks.event: Light is divided from darkness
event_checks.reason: Genesis 1:3-5 states God divided the light from the darkness on the first day.

event_checks.event: The firmament divides the waters
event_checks.reason: Genesis 1:6-8 describes the firmament dividing the waters under from the waters above on the second day.

event_checks.event: Dry land appears and plants grow
event_checks.reason: Genesis 1:9-13 has the dry land appear and the earth bring forth grass, herbs and fruit trees on the third day.

event_checks.event: The sun, moon and stars are set in the sky
event_checks.reason: Genesis 1:14-19 says God made the greater and lesser lights and the stars and set them in the firmament on the fourth day. Calling these the sun and moon is a standard paraphrase.

event_checks.event: Sea creatures and birds are created
event_checks.reason: Genesis 1:20-23 describes the creation of water creatures, great whales and winged fowl on the fifth day.

event_checks.event: Jacob is born holding Esau's heel
event_checks.reason: Genesis 25:26 states his hand took hold on Esau's heel and he was named Jacob.

event_checks.event: Esau sells his birthright for pottage
event_checks.reason: Genesis 25:33-34 records Esau selling his birthright and Jacob giving him bread and pottage of lentiles.

event_checks.event: Jacob dreams of a ladder to heaven
event_checks.reason: Genesis 28:12 describes a ladder set up on earth with its top reaching to heaven.

event_checks.event: Jacob wrestles and is renamed Israel
event_checks.reason: Genesis 32:24-28 records the wrestling and the renaming to Israel.

event_checks.event: God tells Noah to build an ark of gopher wood
event_checks.reason: Genesis 6:14 says, "Make thee an ark of gopher wood."

event_checks.event: Noah's family and the animals go into the ark
event_checks.reason: Genesis 7:7-9 describes Noah, his wife, his sons and his sons' wives, together with the animals two and two, going into the ark.

event_checks.event: Rain falls for forty days and forty nights
event_checks.reason: Genesis 7:12 states this directly. Rain falling after the entry into the ark is consistent with the narrative.

event_checks.event: A dove returns with an olive leaf
event_checks.reason: Genesis 8:11 says the dove came in with an olive leaf in her mouth.

event_checks.event: God sets His bow in the cloud as a covenant sign
event_checks.reason: Genesis 9:13 says, "I do set my bow in the cloud... for a token of a covenant."

event_checks.event: God calls Abram to leave his country
event_checks.reason: Genesis 12:1 records the LORD telling Abram to get out of his country, his kindred and his father's house.

event_checks.event: God promises descendants like the stars
event_checks.reason: Genesis 15:5 has God telling Abram to count the stars and saying 'So shall thy seed be.'

event_checks.event: Abram's name is changed to Abraham
event_checks.reason: Genesis 17:5 states his name shall no longer be Abram but Abraham.

event_checks.event: Isaac is born to Sarah
event_checks.reason: Genesis 21:2-3 records that Sarah bare Abraham a son, who was named Isaac.

event_checks.event: Abraham is tested in the land of Moriah
event_checks.reason: Genesis 22:1-2 says God did tempt (test) Abraham and told him to go to the land of Moriah to offer Isaac. The order also matches the chapter sequence.

event_checks.event: Baby Moses is placed among the bulrushes
event_checks.reason: Exodus 2:3 says his mother put him in an ark of bulrushes and laid it in the flags (reeds) by the river's brink. That is an acceptable paraphrase.

event_checks.event: God speaks from the burning bush
event_checks.reason: Exodus 3:4 says God called unto him out of the midst of the bush that burned but was not consumed.

event_checks.event: The river is turned to blood
event_checks.reason: Exodus 7:20 says all the waters in the river were turned to blood.

event_checks.event: The first Passover is kept
event_checks.reason: Exodus 12:21-23 gives the Passover instructions, and 12:28 records that Israel did as commanded.

event_checks.event: Israel crosses the Red Sea on dry ground
event_checks.reason: Exodus 14:22 says Israel went into the midst of the sea upon dry ground. The verse says only 'the sea', but naming it the Red Sea fits the surrounding narrative (e.g., Exodus 13:18, 15:4).

event_checks.event: An angel appears to Gideon by the winepress
event_checks.reason: Judges 6:11-12 says the angel of the LORD appeared to Gideon while he threshed wheat by the winepress.

event_checks.event: Gideon tests God with a fleece
event_checks.reason: Judges 6:36-40 describes the two fleece tests, which come after the angel's appearance.

event_checks.event: God reduces the army to three hundred
event_checks.reason: Judges 7:4-7 describes the water test and God choosing the three hundred who lapped.

event_checks.event: Trumpets sound and pitchers are broken
event_checks.reason: Judges 7:20 states the companies blew the trumpets and brake the pitchers.

event_checks.event: Rahab hides the spies in Jericho
event_checks.reason: Joshua 2:1-4 states the two spies lodged in Rahab's house in Jericho and she hid them.

event_checks.event: Israel crosses the Jordan on dry ground
event_checks.reason: Joshua 3:17 says all the Israelites passed over on dry ground.

event_checks.event: The walls of Jericho fall
event_checks.reason: Joshua 6:20 says the wall fell down flat after the shout and the trumpets.

event_checks.event: The sun stands still at Gibeon
event_checks.reason: Joshua 10:12-13 has Joshua command, 'Sun, stand thou still upon Gibeon,' and the sun stood still.

event_checks.event: Jacob gives Joseph a coat of many colours
event_checks.reason: Genesis 37:3 says Israel (Jacob) made Joseph a coat of many colours.

event_checks.event: Joseph's brothers sell him for twenty pieces of silver
event_checks.reason: Judah proposes selling Joseph and the brothers agree. Verse 28's 'they drew… and sold Joseph… for twenty pieces of silver' is grammatically ambiguous, since 'they' could mean the Midianites. Genesis 45:4 ('whom ye sold') does attribute the sale to the brothers, so the description is defensible but slightly firmer than verse 28 alone.

event_checks.event: Joseph serves in Potiphar's house
event_checks.reason: Genesis 39:1-4 says Potiphar bought Joseph, Joseph served him, and he was made overseer of his house.

event_checks.event: Joseph interprets Pharaoh's dream
event_checks.reason: Genesis 41:25-30 has Joseph explaining Pharaoh's dream as seven years of plenty followed by seven years of famine.

event_checks.event: Joseph reveals himself to his brothers
event_checks.reason: Genesis 45:4 has Joseph say 'I am Joseph your brother, whom ye sold into Egypt.'

event_checks.event: Waters turned to blood
event_checks.reason: Exodus 7:20 states that all the waters in the river were turned to blood.

event_checks.event: Frogs cover the land
event_checks.reason: Exodus 8:6 says the frogs came up and covered the land of Egypt.

event_checks.event: Dust becomes lice
event_checks.reason: Exodus 8:17 says the dust of the earth became lice throughout all the land of Egypt.

event_checks.event: Thick darkness for three days
event_checks.reason: Exodus 10:22 says there was a thick darkness in all the land of Egypt three days.

event_checks.event: Death of the firstborn
event_checks.reason: Exodus 12:29 says the LORD smote all the firstborn in the land of Egypt at midnight.

event_checks.event: God provides manna
event_checks.reason: Exodus 16:14-15 describes the small round thing on the ground, which the people called manna, and Moses identifies it as bread given by the LORD.

event_checks.event: The Ten Commandments are given at Sinai
event_checks.reason: Exodus 19:20 places the LORD on mount Sinai, and Exodus 20:1-3 begins God speaking the commandments.

event_checks.event: The people make a golden calf
event_checks.reason: Exodus 32:1-4 shows the people demanding gods and supplying their golden earrings, and Aaron fashioning a molten calf. Crediting the people is a fair paraphrase; Exodus 32:35 itself says 'they made the calf, which Aaron made.'

event_checks.event: Twelve spies are sent to search Canaan
event_checks.reason: Numbers 13:1-3 and 13:17 describe Moses sending one man from every tribe to search Canaan. The number twelve follows from 'every tribe' and the list of twelve names in the chapter.

event_checks.event: An angel announces a Nazarite son
event_checks.reason: Judges 13:3-5 has the angel of the LORD telling the barren woman she will bear a son who will be a Nazarite unto God from the womb.

event_checks.event: Samson tears a young lion
event_checks.reason: Judges 14:5-6 says Samson 'rent him as he would have rent a kid' when a young lion roared against him.

event_checks.event: Samson loves Delilah
event_checks.reason: Judges 16:4 says 'he loved a woman in the valley of Sorek, whose name was Delilah.'

event_checks.event: Samson brings down the house
event_checks.reason: Judges 16:30 says he bowed himself with all his might and the house fell upon the lords and all the people.

event_checks.event: Ruth vows to go with Naomi
event_checks.reason: Ruth 1:16-17 records Ruth's vow: 'whither thou goest, I will go.'

event_checks.event: Ruth gleans in the field of Boaz
event_checks.reason: Ruth 2:3 says she gleaned on a part of the field belonging unto Boaz.

event_checks.event: Ruth asks Boaz to spread his skirt over her
event_checks.reason: Ruth 3:9 records her request directly.

event_checks.event: Boaz marries Ruth
event_checks.reason: Ruth 4:13: 'Boaz took Ruth, and she was his wife.'

event_checks.event: Obed is born
event_checks.reason: Ruth 4:13 records the birth of a son, and Ruth 4:17 names him Obed.

event_checks.event: Hannah prays and makes a vow
event_checks.reason: 1 Samuel 1:10-11 records that Hannah prayed and wept, then vowed to give a son to the LORD.

event_checks.event: The LORD calls the boy Samuel
event_checks.reason: 1 Samuel 3:8-10 records the LORD calling Samuel, who is called 'the child', and Samuel answering.

event_checks.event: Samuel anoints Saul
event_checks.reason: 1 Samuel 10:1 says Samuel poured oil on Saul's head and declared that the LORD had anointed him captain.

event_checks.event: Samuel anoints David
event_checks.reason: 1 Samuel 16:13 says Samuel anointed David with the horn of oil among his brethren.

event_checks.event: Samuel anoints David
event_checks.reason: 1 Samuel 16:13 states that Samuel took the horn of oil and anointed him.

event_checks.event: David plays the harp for Saul
event_checks.reason: 1 Samuel 16:23 states that David took an harp and played, and Saul was refreshed.

event_checks.event: David defeats Goliath
event_checks.reason: 1 Samuel 17:4 names Goliath as the Philistine champion, and 17:48-50 describes David slaying him with a sling and a stone.

event_checks.event: David spares Saul in the cave
event_checks.reason: 1 Samuel 24:3-7 shows David cutting Saul's skirt but refusing to harm the LORD's anointed, and Saul leaving the cave unharmed.

event_checks.event: David is anointed king over Israel
event_checks.reason: 2 Samuel 5:3 states that the elders anointed David king over Israel in Hebron.

event_checks.event: Solomon asks for an understanding heart
event_checks.reason: 1 Kings 3:9 records Solomon asking for an understanding heart to judge the people.

event_checks.event: Solomon judges between two mothers
event_checks.reason: 1 Kings 3:16-27 describes two women coming before the king and his judgment that the one who would spare the child is the mother.

event_checks.event: Solomon builds the house of the LORD
event_checks.reason: 1 Kings 6:1 and 6:14 state that Solomon began building the house of the LORD and finished it.

event_checks.event: The temple is dedicated
event_checks.reason: 1 Kings 8:63 says the king and all Israel dedicated the house of the LORD.

event_checks.event: The queen of Sheba visits
event_checks.reason: 1 Kings 10:1-2 describes the queen of Sheba coming to Jerusalem to prove Solomon.

event_checks.event: Ravens feed Elijah
event_checks.reason: 1 Kings 17:6 states the ravens brought him bread and flesh morning and evening.

event_checks.event: The widow's meal and oil do not run out
event_checks.reason: 1 Kings 17:16: the barrel of meal wasted not, neither did the cruse of oil fail.

event_checks.event: Fire falls on Mount Carmel
event_checks.reason: 1 Kings 18:20 places the event at Mount Carmel, and 18:38 says the fire of the LORD fell.

event_checks.event: Elijah hears a still small voice
event_checks.reason: 1 Kings 19:12-13: after the fire came a still small voice, and Elijah heard it.

event_checks.event: Elijah goes up by a whirlwind
event_checks.reason: 2 Kings 2:11: Elijah went up by a whirlwind into heaven.

event_checks.event: Daniel refuses the king's meat
event_checks.reason: Daniel 1:8 states Daniel purposed not to defile himself with the king's meat and asked to be excused from it.

event_checks.event: Daniel interprets the dream of the great image
event_checks.reason: Daniel 2:31-32 describes the image, and 2:36-38 begins the interpretation ("Thou art this head of gold").

event_checks.event: Three friends are cast into the furnace
event_checks.reason: Daniel 3:20-23 says Shadrach, Meshach and Abed-nego were bound and cast into the burning fiery furnace.

event_checks.event: Fingers write on the palace wall
event_checks.reason: Daniel 5:5 says fingers of a man's hand wrote upon the plaister of the wall of the king's palace.

event_checks.event: Daniel is cast into the den of lions
event_checks.reason: Daniel 6:16 says they brought Daniel and cast him into the den of lions.

event_checks.event: Esther is made queen
event_checks.reason: Esther 2:17 says the king set the royal crown on her head and made her queen instead of Vashti.

event_checks.event: Haman plots against the Jews
event_checks.reason: Esther 3:6 says Haman sought to destroy all the Jews throughout Ahasuerus's kingdom.

event_checks.event: Esther goes in to the king
event_checks.reason: Esther 5:1-2 describes Esther standing in the inner court, the king holding out the sceptre, and Esther drawing near.

event_checks.event: Haman is hanged on his own gallows
event_checks.reason: Esther 7:10 says Haman was hanged on the gallows he had prepared for Mordecai. 'His own gallows' is a fair paraphrase.

event_checks.event: God calls Jonah to go to Nineveh
event_checks.reason: Jonah 1:1-2 records the LORD telling Jonah to arise and go to Nineveh and cry against it.

event_checks.event: Jonah flees toward Tarshish
event_checks.reason: Jonah 1:3 says Jonah rose up to flee unto Tarshish and boarded a ship going there.

event_checks.event: A great fish swallows Jonah
event_checks.reason: Jonah 1:17 says the LORD prepared a great fish to swallow up Jonah.

event_checks.event: Jonah warns Nineveh: forty days
event_checks.reason: Jonah 3:4 records Jonah crying, 'Yet forty days, and Nineveh shall be overthrown.'

event_checks.event: God prepares a gourd to shade Jonah
event_checks.reason: Jonah 4:6 says the LORD God prepared a gourd to be a shadow over Jonah's head.

event_checks.event: The women find the stone rolled away
event_checks.reason: Luke 24:1-3 states they found the stone rolled away, and 24:10 identifies them as women (Mary Magdalene, Joanna, Mary the mother of James, and others).

event_checks.event: Two disciples walk to Emmaus
event_checks.reason: Luke 24:13 says two of them went that same day to a village called Emmaus.

event_checks.event: Jesus stands among the disciples: Peace be unto you
event_checks.reason: Luke 24:36 says Jesus himself stood in the midst of them and said, Peace be unto you.

event_checks.event: Jesus is carried up into heaven
event_checks.reason: Luke 24:51 says he was parted from them and carried up into heaven.

event_checks.event: Jesus is baptized
event_checks.reason: Matthew 3:16 explicitly states Jesus was baptized and came up out of the water.

event_checks.event: Jesus is tempted in the wilderness
event_checks.reason: Matthew 4:1 states Jesus was led into the wilderness to be tempted of the devil. It begins with 'Then', which follows the baptism.

event_checks.event: Jesus calls fishermen to be fishers of men
event_checks.reason: Matthew 4:18-20 shows Jesus calling Simon Peter and Andrew, who were fishers, saying 'I will make you fishers of men.'

event_checks.event: Jesus teaches on the mountain
event_checks.reason: Matthew 5:1-2 says he went up into a mountain and taught them. It follows chapter 4 in Matthew's narrative.

event_checks.event: Gabriel announces Jesus' birth to Mary
event_checks.reason: Luke 1:26-31 records Gabriel sent to Mary in Nazareth, telling her she will conceive and bear a son named JESUS.

event_checks.event: Joseph and Mary travel to Bethlehem
event_checks.reason: Luke 2:4-5 says Joseph went up from Nazareth to Bethlehem to be taxed with Mary, who was great with child.

event_checks.event: Angels appear to shepherds
event_checks.reason: Luke 2:8-14 says the angel of the Lord appeared to the shepherds, followed by a multitude of the heavenly host. That supports the plural 'angels'.

event_checks.event: Simeon holds the child in the temple
event_checks.reason: Luke 2:25-28 says Simeon came into the temple and took the child Jesus up in his arms.

event_checks.event: The twelve-year-old Jesus is found in the temple
event_checks.reason: Luke 2:42-46 says that when Jesus was twelve, his parents found him in the temple after three days.

event_checks.event: Crowds cry Hosanna as Jesus enters Jerusalem
event_checks.reason: Matthew 21:9-10 records the multitudes crying Hosanna as he came into Jerusalem.

event_checks.event: Jesus breaks bread at the Last Supper
event_checks.reason: Matthew 26:26 says Jesus took bread, blessed it, and brake it while they were eating. 'Last Supper' is a traditional label for this meal.

event_checks.event: Jesus prays in Gethsemane
event_checks.reason: Matthew 26:36-39 explicitly describes Jesus praying at Gethsemane.

event_checks.event: Jesus is crucified
event_checks.reason: Matthew 27:35 states 'they crucified him'.

event_checks.event: The angel says: He is not here, for he is risen
event_checks.reason: Matthew 28:6 quotes the angel's words nearly verbatim.

event_checks.event: A traveller falls among thieves
event_checks.reason: Luke 10:30 says a certain man going from Jerusalem to Jericho fell among thieves.

event_checks.event: A priest passes by
event_checks.reason: Luke 10:31 says the priest passed by on the other side.

event_checks.event: A Levite passes by
event_checks.reason: Luke 10:32 says the Levite likewise passed by on the other side.

event_checks.event: A Samaritan binds up his wounds
event_checks.reason: Luke 10:34 says he bound up his wounds, pouring in oil and wine.

event_checks.event: He pays the host two pence
event_checks.reason: Luke 10:35 says he took out two pence and gave them to the host.

event_checks.event: Jesus is taken up in a cloud
event_checks.reason: Acts 1:9 states he was taken up and a cloud received him out of their sight.

event_checks.event: The Spirit comes at Pentecost
event_checks.reason: Acts 2:1-4 describes the day of Pentecost and their being filled with the Holy Ghost.

event_checks.event: A lame man is healed at the temple gate
event_checks.reason: Acts 3:2-8 describes a man lame from birth at the Beautiful gate who is healed and walks.

event_checks.event: Stephen is stoned
event_checks.reason: Acts 7:59 states they stoned Stephen.

event_checks.event: Saul meets the risen Jesus near Damascus
event_checks.reason: Acts 9:3-5 describes Saul near Damascus hearing the Lord say 'I am Jesus.' 'Risen' is a reasonable inference, since Jesus speaks from heaven after the ascension.

event_checks.event: Saul is converted near Damascus
event_checks.reason: Acts 9:3-6 describes the light from heaven near Damascus and Saul's encounter with Jesus, whom he calls Lord.

event_checks.event: Barnabas and Saul are separated for the work
event_checks.reason: Acts 13:2 records the Holy Ghost saying, 'Separate me Barnabas and Saul for the work.'

event_checks.event: Paul sees a vision of a man of Macedonia
event_checks.reason: Acts 16:9 matches the description directly.

event_checks.event: Paul preaches on Mars' hill in Athens
event_checks.reason: Acts 17:22 has Paul standing on Mars' hill and addressing the men of Athens.

event_checks.event: Paul is shipwrecked on Melita
event_checks.reason: Acts 27:41-44 describes the ship running aground and breaking up. Acts 28:1 names the island as Melita.

event_checks.event: All the earth has one language
event_checks.reason: Genesis 11:1 states the whole earth was of one language and one speech.

event_checks.event: People settle in a plain in the land of Shinar
event_checks.reason: Genesis 11:2 says they found a plain in Shinar and dwelt there.

event_checks.event: They make brick and plan a city and a tower
event_checks.reason: Genesis 11:3-4 describes making brick and proposing to build a city and a tower.

event_checks.event: The LORD comes down to see the city
event_checks.reason: Genesis 11:5 says the LORD came down to see the city and the tower.

event_checks.event: Their language is confounded and they are scattered
event_checks.reason: Genesis 11:7-9 describes the confounding of language and the scattering abroad.

event_checks.event: Abel keeps sheep and Cain tills the ground
event_checks.reason: Genesis 4:2 states Abel was a keeper of sheep and Cain a tiller of the ground.

event_checks.event: Both bring offerings to the LORD
event_checks.reason: Genesis 4:3-4 records Cain bringing fruit of the ground and Abel bringing firstlings of his flock.

event_checks.event: God warns Cain that sin lieth at the door
event_checks.reason: Genesis 4:6-7 has the LORD telling Cain that if he does not well, sin lieth at the door.

event_checks.event: Cain rises up against Abel in the field
event_checks.reason: Genesis 4:8 says that when they were in the field, Cain rose up against Abel and slew him.

event_checks.event: God sets a mark upon Cain
event_checks.reason: Genesis 4:15 says the LORD set a mark upon Cain, lest any finding him should kill him.

event_checks.event: The younger son asks for his portion
event_checks.reason: Luke 15:12 records the younger son asking, 'Father, give me the portion of goods that falleth to me.'

event_checks.event: He wastes his substance with riotous living
event_checks.reason: Luke 15:13 says he 'wasted his substance with riotous living.'

event_checks.event: He feeds swine in a far country
event_checks.reason: Luke 15:13-15 places him in a far country, where a citizen 'sent him into his fields to feed swine.'

event_checks.event: His father runs to embrace him
event_checks.reason: Luke 15:20 says the father 'ran, and fell on his neck, and kissed him.' Running to embrace him is a fair paraphrase.

event_checks.event: The elder brother is angry
event_checks.reason: Luke 15:28 says 'he was angry, and would not go in.'

event_checks.event: Rahab hides the two spies
event_checks.reason: Joshua 2:4-6 states she took the two men and hid them with the stalks of flax on the roof.

event_checks.event: Israel crosses the Jordan on dry ground
event_checks.reason: Joshua 3:17 says all the Israelites passed over on dry ground.

event_checks.event: The people march around the city once a day for six days
event_checks.reason: Joshua 6:11-14 describes compassing the city once and returning to camp, 'so they did six days.'

event_checks.event: On the seventh day they compass the city seven times
event_checks.reason: Joshua 6:15 explicitly states this.

event_checks.event: The wall falls down flat
event_checks.reason: Joshua 6:20 says the wall fell down flat after the shout.

event_checks.event: God tells Abraham to take Isaac to the land of Moriah
event_checks.reason: Gen 22:2 states God told Abraham to take Isaac and get into the land of Moriah.

event_checks.event: Abraham rises early and saddles his ass
event_checks.reason: Gen 22:3 says Abraham rose up early in the morning and saddled his ass.

event_checks.event: Isaac asks where the lamb is
event_checks.reason: Gen 22:7 records Isaac asking where the lamb for a burnt offering is.

event_checks.event: The angel of the LORD calls out of heaven
event_checks.reason: Gen 22:11 says the angel of the LORD called unto him out of heaven.

event_checks.event: A ram caught in a thicket is offered instead
event_checks.reason: Gen 22:13 says Abraham offered the ram caught in a thicket in the stead of his son.

event_checks.event: Israel camps before the mount
event_checks.reason: Exodus 19:2 explicitly states Israel camped before the mount after coming to the desert of Sinai.

event_checks.event: Mount Sinai smokes as the LORD descends
event_checks.reason: Exodus 19:18 says Sinai was altogether on a smoke because the LORD descended upon it in fire.

event_checks.event: God speaks the ten commandments
event_checks.reason: Exodus 20:1 says God spake all these words, beginning the commandments, and Deuteronomy 4:13 identifies them as the ten commandments.

event_checks.event: The people make a golden calf
event_checks.reason: Exodus 32:1-4 shows the people demanding gods and bringing their gold, with Aaron fashioning a molten calf. Attributing it to the people is a fair paraphrase, and Exodus 32:35 itself says 'they made the calf.'

event_checks.event: Moses hews two new tables of stone
event_checks.reason: Exodus 34:1-4 says the LORD commanded Moses to hew two tables like the first, and that he hewed them.

event_checks.event: Hannah prays in bitterness of soul at Shiloh
event_checks.reason: 1 Sam 1:9-10 states she was in bitterness of soul and prayed unto the LORD at Shiloh.

event_checks.event: Eli thinks she is drunken
event_checks.reason: 1 Sam 1:13 says Eli thought she had been drunken.

event_checks.event: Hannah bears a son and names him Samuel
event_checks.reason: 1 Sam 1:20 says she bare a son and called his name Samuel.

event_checks.event: She lends the child to the LORD
event_checks.reason: 1 Sam 1:28 says 'I have lent him to the LORD.'

event_checks.event: Hannah prays: My heart rejoiceth in the LORD
event_checks.reason: 1 Sam 2:1 quotes these words directly, and they follow 1:28.

event_checks.event: A little maid tells of the prophet in Samaria
event_checks.reason: In 2 Kings 5:2-3 the captive maid tells her mistress about the prophet in Samaria, who would recover Naaman of his leprosy.

event_checks.event: The king of Israel rends his clothes
event_checks.reason: 2 Kings 5:7 says the king of Israel rent his clothes after reading the letter.

event_checks.event: Elisha says to wash in Jordan seven times
event_checks.reason: 2 Kings 5:10 has Elisha send a messenger telling Naaman to wash in Jordan seven times. The message came through a messenger, which the paraphrase allows.

event_checks.event: Naaman turns away in a rage
event_checks.reason: 2 Kings 5:12 says 'So he turned and went away in a rage.'

event_checks.event: His flesh comes again like a little child's
event_checks.reason: 2 Kings 5:14 says his flesh 'came again like unto the flesh of a little child.'

event_checks.event: The sisters send word that Lazarus is sick
event_checks.reason: John 11:3 states his sisters sent unto him saying he whom thou lovest is sick.

event_checks.event: Jesus arrives after Lazarus has lain in the grave four days
event_checks.reason: John 11:17 says when Jesus came he found Lazarus had lain in the grave four days already.

event_checks.event: Jesus says: I am the resurrection, and the life
event_checks.reason: John 11:25 quotes this exactly.

event_checks.event: Jesus weeps
event_checks.reason: John 11:35: Jesus wept.

event_checks.event: Lazarus comes forth bound with graveclothes
event_checks.reason: John 11:44 says he came forth bound hand and foot with graveclothes.

event_checks.event: Nehemiah weeps over the news of Jerusalem
event_checks.reason: Nehemiah 1:4 says that when he heard these words he sat down, wept and mourned.

event_checks.event: King Artaxerxes asks why his countenance is sad
event_checks.reason: Nehemiah 2:1-2 names Artaxerxes, who asks, 'Why is thy countenance sad?'

event_checks.event: Nehemiah views the walls by night
event_checks.reason: Nehemiah 2:13 says he went out by night and viewed the walls of Jerusalem.

event_checks.event: Sanballat and Tobiah mock the builders
event_checks.reason: Nehemiah 4:1-3 has Sanballat mocking the Jews, and Tobiah adds his own taunt about the fox breaking down the wall.

event_checks.event: The wall is finished in fifty and two days
event_checks.reason: Nehemiah 6:15 states the wall was finished in fifty and two days.

event_checks.event: Pharaoh orders every son born to be cast into the river
event_checks.reason: Exodus 1:22 states Pharaoh charged all his people that every son born be cast into the river.

event_checks.event: Baby Moses is hidden in an ark of bulrushes
event_checks.reason: The text says she hid him for three months, and only 'when she could not longer hide him' did she put him in an ark of bulrushes among the flags. Saying he was 'hidden in' the ark loosely merges the two steps. The child is also not yet named Moses in these verses, though that is acceptable context.

event_checks.event: Pharaoh's daughter finds the child
event_checks.reason: Exodus 2:5-6 describes Pharaoh's daughter seeing the ark, having it fetched, and finding the child.

event_checks.event: Moses flees to the land of Midian
event_checks.reason: Exodus 2:15 states Moses fled from Pharaoh and dwelt in the land of Midian.

event_checks.event: God speaks from the burning bush
event_checks.reason: Exodus 3:2-4 records the bush burning without being consumed and God calling to Moses out of the midst of the bush.

event_checks.event: Nebuchadnezzar sets up an image of gold
event_checks.reason: Daniel 3:1 states he made an image of gold and set it up in the plain of Dura.

event_checks.event: Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego refuse to worship it
event_checks.reason: Daniel 3:12 and 3:18 show they neither served his gods nor worshipped the golden image.

event_checks.event: The furnace is heated seven times hotter
event_checks.reason: Daniel 3:19 says to heat it 'one seven times more than it was wont to be heated,' which is a fair paraphrase.

event_checks.event: The king sees four men loose in the fire
event_checks.reason: Daniel 3:25: 'Lo, I see four men loose, walking in the midst of the fire.'

event_checks.event: They come out with no smell of fire upon them
event_checks.reason: Daniel 3:26-27 records them coming forth and says 'nor the smell of fire had passed on them.'

event_checks.event: A great multitude follows Jesus
event_checks.reason: John 6:2 states a great multitude followed him.

event_checks.event: Jesus asks Philip where to buy bread
event_checks.reason: John 6:5 records Jesus asking Philip, 'Whence shall we buy bread?'

event_checks.event: Andrew tells Jesus of a lad with five barley loaves and two small fishes
event_checks.reason: John 6:8-9 has Andrew mention the lad with five barley loaves and two small fishes.

event_checks.event: The men sit down and Jesus gives thanks
event_checks.reason: John 6:10-11 says the men sat down and Jesus gave thanks before distributing.

event_checks.event: Twelve baskets of fragments are gathered
event_checks.reason: John 6:12-13 says they filled twelve baskets with the fragments.

event_checks.event: Saul consents to Stephen's death
event_checks.reason: Acts 8:1 states 'Saul was consenting unto his death.'

event_checks.event: A light from heaven shines around Saul near Damascus
event_checks.reason: Acts 9:3 says that near Damascus 'there shined round about him a light from heaven.'

event_checks.event: Saul is three days without sight
event_checks.reason: Acts 9:9 says 'he was three days without sight.'

event_checks.event: Ananias lays his hands on Saul
event_checks.reason: Acts 9:17 says Ananias was 'putting his hands on him.'

event_checks.event: Saul preaches Christ in the synagogues
event_checks.reason: Acts 9:20 says 'he preached Christ in the synagogues.'

event_checks.event: Lot chooses the plain of Jordan
event_checks.reason: Genesis 13:11 states Lot chose all the plain of Jordan.

event_checks.event: Abram hears that Lot was taken captive
event_checks.reason: Genesis 14:14 says Abram heard his brother was taken captive.

event_checks.event: Two angels come to Sodom at evening
event_checks.reason: Genesis 19:1 says two angels came to Sodom at even.

event_checks.event: Lot's wife looks back
event_checks.reason: Genesis 19:26 says his wife looked back and became a pillar of salt.

event_checks.event: Abraham sends his servant to his kindred
event_checks.reason: Gen 24:4 has Abraham charging the servant to go to his country and kindred to take a wife for Isaac.

event_checks.event: Rebekah offers to water the camels
event_checks.reason: Gen 24:19: 'I will draw water for thy camels also.'

event_checks.event: Laban runs out to the man at the well
event_checks.reason: Gen 24:29 states this directly.

event_checks.event: Rebekah says, I will go
event_checks.reason: Gen 24:58 quotes her words exactly.

event_checks.event: Rebekah becomes Isaac's wife
event_checks.reason: Gen 24:67: 'she became his wife.'

event_checks.event: Ten brothers go down to buy corn in Egypt
event_checks.reason: Genesis 42:3 states this directly.

event_checks.event: Simeon is bound before their eyes
event_checks.reason: Genesis 42:24 says Joseph took Simeon and bound him before their eyes.

event_checks.event: The brothers take Benjamin down to Egypt
event_checks.reason: Genesis 43:15 says they took Benjamin and went down to Egypt.

event_checks.event: The cup is found in Benjamin's sack
event_checks.reason: Genesis 44:12 says the cup was found in Benjamin's sack.

event_checks.event: Joseph makes himself known
event_checks.reason: Genesis 45:1-3 says Joseph made himself known unto his brethren.

event_checks.event: Jacob waters Rachel's flock at the well
event_checks.reason: Genesis 29:9-10 says Rachel came with her father's sheep, which she kept, and Jacob rolled the stone away and watered Laban's flock. Calling it 'Rachel's flock' is a fair paraphrase.

event_checks.event: Jacob serves seven years for Rachel
event_checks.reason: Genesis 29:20 states this directly.

event_checks.event: Jacob finds he has married Leah
event_checks.reason: Genesis 29:25 says that in the morning, 'behold, it was Leah'.

event_checks.event: Jacob serves seven more years
event_checks.reason: Genesis 29:30 says he 'served with him yet seven other years'.

event_checks.event: Moses sends the spies to search Canaan
event_checks.reason: Numbers 13:17 states Moses sent them to spy out the land of Canaan.

event_checks.event: Two men carry a cluster of grapes on a staff
event_checks.reason: Numbers 13:23 says they bare the cluster 'between two upon a staff.'

event_checks.event: Caleb says, Let us go up at once
event_checks.reason: Numbers 13:30 quotes Caleb exactly.

event_checks.event: The people murmur against Moses and Aaron
event_checks.reason: Numbers 14:2 states all Israel murmured against Moses and Aaron.

event_checks.event: Israel must wander forty years
event_checks.reason: Numbers 14:33-34 declares the children shall wander forty years and the people bear their iniquities forty years.

event_checks.event: Zacchaeus, a chief among the publicans, seeks to see Jesus
event_checks.reason: Luke 19:2-3 calls him 'the chief among the publicans' and says he 'sought to see Jesus.'

event_checks.event: He climbs up into a sycomore tree
event_checks.reason: Luke 19:4 says he 'climbed up into a sycomore tree to see him.'

event_checks.event: Jesus says: to day I must abide at thy house
event_checks.reason: This is a direct quote from Luke 19:5.

event_checks.event: The people murmur
event_checks.reason: Luke 19:7 says 'they all murmured' that he was gone to be guest with a sinner.

event_checks.event: Zacchaeus gives half his goods to the poor
event_checks.reason: Luke 19:8 records Zacchaeus declaring 'the half of my goods I give to the poor.' The text gives his statement, not a narrated act of distribution. 'Declares he gives' would be more precise, but the paraphrase is close.

event_checks.event: Balaam saddles his ass and goes with the princes of Moab
event_checks.reason: Numbers 22:21 states this directly.

event_checks.event: The ass sees the angel standing in the way
event_checks.reason: Numbers 22:23 says the ass saw the angel of the LORD standing in the way.

event_checks.event: The LORD opens the mouth of the ass
event_checks.reason: Numbers 22:28 says the LORD opened the mouth of the ass.

event_checks.event: The LORD opens Balaam's eyes
event_checks.reason: Numbers 22:31 says the LORD opened the eyes of Balaam.

event_checks.event: Balak complains that Balaam has blessed Israel
event_checks.reason: Numbers 23:11: Balak protests that Balaam has 'blessed them altogether', meaning his enemies, Israel. That is a fair paraphrase.

event_checks.event: Absalom steals the hearts of the men of Israel
event_checks.reason: 2 Samuel 15:6 states 'so Absalom stole the hearts of the men of Israel.'

event_checks.event: David flees from Jerusalem
event_checks.reason: 2 Samuel 15:14-16 records David saying 'Arise, and let us flee' and going forth with his household.

event_checks.event: Absalom's head is caught in an oak
event_checks.reason: 2 Samuel 18:9 says 'his head caught hold of the oak.'

event_checks.event: Joab thrusts three darts into Absalom
event_checks.reason: 2 Samuel 18:14 says Joab took three darts and thrust them through Absalom's heart.

event_checks.event: David weeps, O my son Absalom
event_checks.reason: 2 Samuel 18:33 records David weeping and saying 'O my son Absalom.'

event_checks.event: Deborah judges Israel under the palm tree
event_checks.reason: Judges 4:4-5 says she judged Israel and dwelt under the palm tree, where Israel came to her for judgment.

event_checks.event: Deborah calls Barak to Mount Tabor
event_checks.reason: Judges 4:6 says she called Barak and told him to draw toward mount Tabor. This is a fair paraphrase.

event_checks.event: Barak goes down from Mount Tabor
event_checks.reason: Judges 4:14 says Barak went down from mount Tabor with ten thousand men.

event_checks.event: Jael drives a nail through Sisera's temples
event_checks.reason: Judges 4:21 says she smote the nail into his temples and fastened it into the ground. 'Through' is a minor paraphrase.

event_checks.event: Deborah and Barak sing a song
event_checks.reason: Judges 5:1 says Deborah and Barak sang on that day.

event_checks.event: The elders ask Samuel for a king
event_checks.reason: 1 Samuel 8:4-5 states the elders came to Samuel at Ramah and said, "make us a king to judge us."

event_checks.event: Saul, a choice young man, is introduced
event_checks.reason: 1 Samuel 9:1-2 introduces Saul son of Kish as "a choice young man, and a goodly."

event_checks.event: Samuel anoints Saul with a vial of oil
event_checks.reason: 1 Samuel 10:1 says Samuel took a vial of oil and poured it upon Saul's head, calling it the LORD's anointing.

event_checks.event: The people shout, God save the king
event_checks.reason: 1 Samuel 10:24 says all the people shouted, "God save the king."

event_checks.event: Samuel tells Saul the LORD has rejected him
event_checks.reason: 1 Samuel 15:23 has Samuel say, "he hath also rejected thee from being king."

event_checks.event: David sees a woman from the roof
event_checks.reason: 2 Samuel 11:2 states that from the roof David saw a woman washing herself.

event_checks.event: David writes to set Uriah in the hottest battle
event_checks.reason: 2 Samuel 11:14-15 records David's letter to Joab telling him to set Uriah in the forefront of the hottest battle.

event_checks.event: Nathan says, Thou art the man
event_checks.reason: 2 Samuel 12:7 quotes Nathan saying exactly this to David.

event_checks.event: David confesses, I have sinned
event_checks.reason: 2 Samuel 12:13 has David saying, 'I have sinned against the LORD.'

event_checks.event: Solomon is born
event_checks.reason: 2 Samuel 12:24 says Bath-sheba bare a son and he called his name Solomon.

event_checks.event: Elisha asks for a double portion of Elijah's spirit
event_checks.reason: 2 Kings 2:9 states Elisha's request for a double portion directly.

event_checks.event: Elisha divides the Jordan with Elijah's mantle
event_checks.reason: 2 Kings 2:13-14 says Elisha smote the waters with Elijah's mantle and they parted.

event_checks.event: The widow's oil flows until the vessels are full
event_checks.reason: 2 Kings 4:1-6 says the oil kept flowing until no vessel remained, then stayed.

event_checks.event: The Shunammite's son sneezes seven times
event_checks.reason: 2 Kings 4:35 says the child sneezed seven times.

event_checks.event: The axe head swims
event_checks.reason: 2 Kings 6:5-6 says the iron did swim.

event_checks.event: Jesus goes up a mountain to pray
event_checks.reason: Matthew 14:23 states he went up into a mountain apart to pray.

event_checks.event: The ship is tossed with waves
event_checks.reason: Matthew 14:24 says the ship was tossed with waves, for the wind was contrary.

event_checks.event: Jesus comes walking on the sea
event_checks.reason: Matthew 14:25 says Jesus went unto them, walking on the sea, in the fourth watch.

event_checks.event: Peter begins to sink and cries, Lord, save me
event_checks.reason: Matthew 14:30 says that, beginning to sink, Peter cried, Lord, save me.

event_checks.event: The wind ceases when they come into the ship
event_checks.reason: Matthew 14:32 says the wind ceased when they were come into the ship.

event_checks.event: Josiah becomes king at eight years old
event_checks.reason: 2 Kings 22:1 states Josiah was eight years old when he began to reign.

event_checks.event: The book of the law is found in the temple
event_checks.reason: 2 Kings 22:8 has Hilkiah finding the book of the law in the house of the LORD, which is the temple.

event_checks.event: Josiah tears his clothes
event_checks.reason: 2 Kings 22:11 says the king 'rent his clothes' after hearing the words of the book.

event_checks.event: Josiah makes a covenant before the LORD
event_checks.reason: 2 Kings 23:3 says the king stood by a pillar and made a covenant before the LORD.

event_checks.event: Josiah commands the people to keep the passover
event_checks.reason: 2 Kings 23:21 says the king commanded all the people to keep the passover.

event_checks.event: Cyrus makes a proclamation
event_checks.reason: Ezra 1:1 states Cyrus 'made a proclamation throughout all his kingdom.'

event_checks.event: The foundation of the temple is laid
event_checks.reason: Ezra 3:10-11 describes the builders laying the foundation of the temple, with praise and shouting.

event_checks.event: The people of the land trouble the builders
event_checks.reason: Ezra 4:4 says the people of the land 'troubled them in building.'

event_checks.event: The house of God is finished
event_checks.reason: Ezra 6:15 says the house was finished on the third day of Adar in Darius's sixth year.

event_checks.event: Ezra goes up from Babylon
event_checks.reason: Ezra 7:6 says 'This Ezra went up from Babylon.' It comes after the temple's completion in the narrative (the reign of Artaxerxes).

event_checks.event: Jairus falls at Jesus' feet
event_checks.reason: Mark 5:22 says that when Jairus saw him, he fell at his feet.

event_checks.event: A woman touches Jesus' garment
event_checks.reason: Mark 5:27 says she came in the press behind and touched his garment.

event_checks.event: Jesus asks, Who touched my clothes?
event_checks.reason: Mark 5:30 quotes these words exactly.

event_checks.event: Messengers say, Thy daughter is dead
event_checks.reason: Mark 5:35 says certain men came from the ruler's house and said, Thy daughter is dead. Calling them messengers is a fair paraphrase.

event_checks.event: Jesus says, Talitha cumi
event_checks.reason: Mark 5:41 quotes these words exactly.

event_checks.event: Peter says he is ready to go to prison and to death
event_checks.reason: Luke 22:33 records Peter saying, "I am ready to go with thee, both into prison, and to death."

event_checks.event: Peter follows afar off
event_checks.reason: Luke 22:54 says, "And Peter followed afar off."

event_checks.event: Peter says, Woman, I know him not
event_checks.reason: Luke 22:57 has the exact wording: "Woman, I know him not."

event_checks.event: The Lord turns and looks upon Peter
event_checks.reason: Luke 22:61 says, "And the Lord turned, and looked upon Peter."

event_checks.event: Peter goes out and weeps bitterly
event_checks.reason: Luke 22:62 says, "And Peter went out, and wept bitterly."

event_checks.event: Hezekiah breaks the brasen serpent
event_checks.reason: 2 Kings 18:4 says he 'brake in pieces the brasen serpent that Moses had made.'

event_checks.event: Sennacherib comes up against the fenced cities of Judah
event_checks.reason: 2 Kings 18:13 says that in Hezekiah's fourteenth year Sennacherib came up against all the fenced cities of Judah.

event_checks.event: Hezekiah spreads the letter before the LORD
event_checks.reason: 2 Kings 19:14 says Hezekiah went up into the house of the LORD and spread the letter before the LORD.

event_checks.event: The angel of the LORD strikes the Assyrian camp
event_checks.reason: 2 Kings 19:35 says the angel of the LORD smote 185,000 in the camp of the Assyrians.

event_checks.event: Sennacherib is slain by his sons in his own temple
event_checks.reason: 2 Kings 19:37 says his sons Adrammelech and Sharezer smote him in 'the house of Nisroch his god.' 'His own temple' is a loose paraphrase meaning his god's temple. It is acceptable, though 'in the temple of his god Nisroch' would be more precise. The order follows the narrative in 2 Kings 18–19.

event_checks.event: Stephen is chosen among the seven
event_checks.reason: Acts 6:5 states they chose Stephen first among the seven named men.

event_checks.event: Stephen does great wonders among the people

event_checks.event: Philip asks, Understandest thou what thou readest?

event_checks.event: Rhoda is too glad to open the gate
event_checks.reason: Acts 12:14 says she opened not the gate for gladness. That is a fair paraphrase.

event_checks.event: Cornelius sees an angel in a vision

event_checks.event: Peter sees a great sheet let down from heaven

event_checks.event: The Holy Ghost falls on all who hear

event_checks.event: Peter commands them to be baptized
event_checks.reason: Acts 10:48 says he commanded them to be baptized in the name of the Lord.

event_checks.event: The Lord opens Lydia's heart
event_checks.reason: Acts 16:14 states the Lord opened Lydia's heart.

event_checks.event: Paul casts the spirit out of a damsel
event_checks.reason: Acts 16:18 has Paul command the spirit to come out, and it came out the same hour.

event_checks.event: Paul and Silas are cast into prison
event_checks.reason: Acts 16:23-24 says they were cast into prison and put in the stocks.

event_checks.event: At midnight they pray and sing praises
event_checks.reason: Acts 16:25 matches the description exactly.

event_checks.event: The jailer and all his household are baptized
event_checks.reason: Acts 16:33 says he was baptized, he and all his, straightway. Verse 31 refers to 'thy house', so 'household' is a fair paraphrase.
